title: Nataraja

Sketchfab API /v3/models/6862a3c673d4434a8dc39ced2a5b5720: license.label = 'CC0 Public Domain', license.slug = 'cc0', isDownloadable = true, 98,795 faces / 49,376 vertices. Chosen over the Met's CC0 photograph of its own Nataraja (Met object 39328, 1987.80.1, 68.3 cm) because this is a real scan of a real Chola bronze and is larger; the Met's Sketchfab account (user 'metmuseum') currently lists 0 models, so no Met CC0 3D Nataraja was found. object.description: Shiva as Nataraja, the Lord of Dance (Tamil: நடராஜர், Nataraja; also ஆடவல்லான், Adavallan), cast in bronze in Tamil Nadu in the eleventh century, at the height of the Chola empire. The god dances inside a ring of fire. His upper right hand beats a small drum, the sound that begins creation; his upper left holds the flame that will end it. The lower right hand is raised in the gesture that says 'do not fear', and the lower left points to the lifted foot, where release is found. The other foot presses down on Apasmara, the dwarf of ignorance. The whole figure, with its halo and lotus base, stands over a metre tall and was made by the lost-wax method, in which a wax model is coated in clay, melted out and replaced with molten metal, so each bronze is unique. Images like this were carried in procession at temple festivals, dressed and garlanded. The Nataraja is the most famous form of South Indian art, and the one that Tamil people most readily recognise as their own.
facts: Made in Tamil Nadu under the Chola dynasty, whose bronze-casters produced the finest metal sculpture in India between the 9th and 13th centuries.
Cast by the lost-wax process, so the mould was destroyed and every Chola bronze is a one-off.
The Cleveland Museum of Art scanned the bronze itself and released the model under CC0; it measures 113 by 102 by 30 cm with its ring of fire.
A Nataraja of this type stands outside CERN in Geneva, given by India in 2004 as an image of the cosmic dance of matter.

tour: Shiva as Lord of the Dance, cast in bronze by Chola craftsmen a thousand years ago. The ring of fire is the universe; the dwarf underfoot is ignorance.
